network.tdh.impl.metadataDescription: The Rust core, program B, the Python reference and 6529.io, and how they are checked against each other.
network.tdh.impl.title: Implementations
network.tdh.impl.lede: TDH-v1 is one written rule and several programs, written separately from the same text. They are checked against the same test cases and against each other every day, so a mistake in one shows up as a difference.
network.tdh.impl.programs.title: The programs
network.tdh.impl.programs.caption: Four implementations of TDH, compared
network.tdh.impl.rust.language: Rust, standard library only, integers only
network.tdh.impl.rust.writtenFrom: P26 and the vectors alone, in a clean room; then made into a library with no rule changed
network.tdh.impl.rust.runsIn: Every validator; 6529’s daily job from 16 October; 6529.io from the cutover; proof program A
network.tdh.impl.programB.language: Rust, standard library plus a pinned Keccak crate, integers only
network.tdh.impl.programB.writtenFrom: The specifications alone, in a separate clean room that never read the Rust core, the Python reference or the other Rust code
network.tdh.impl.programB.runsIn: Every validator, as the second check before it signs; proof program B, in a second zero-knowledge virtual machine
network.tdh.impl.python.language: Python 3.10 or later, standard library only, no floating point
network.tdh.impl.python.writtenFrom: Written alongside P26 as its reference
network.tdh.impl.python.runsIn: 6529’s daily job; any validator, as an optional third check
network.tdh.impl.backend.conformance: Measured against TDH-v1 by replay and the daily comparison
network.tdh.impl.lean: A fifth, the Lean model, is in progress.
network.tdh.impl.written.title: How each was written
network.tdh.impl.written.body: The Python reference came first, written with the specification. Then a separate Rust implementation was written from the specification alone, without reading the Python, and it listed every place where it had to guess: 23 in all. The specification now has an exact rule for each, and the vectors pin them.
network.tdh.impl.written.body2: That Rust implementation became the validators’ core without any change to its rules; every copied file is pinned by its hash. Program B was written later, in a separate clean room, from the specifications only.
network.tdh.impl.lineage.title: Where each implementation came from
network.tdh.impl.lineage.desc: The Python reference was written from P26. The clean-room Rust was written from P26 and the vectors only, without reading the Python, and became the Rust core with no rule changed. Program B was written from the specifications only, without reading the Rust core, the Python or the clean-room Rust. The old backend is replaced by the Rust core at the cutover.
network.tdh.impl.lineage.library: made into a library, no rule changed, hash-pinned

network.tdh.impl.where.caption: Where each implementation runs
network.tdh.impl.checked.title: How they are checked
network.tdh.impl.checked.vectors.title: Conformance vectors.
network.tdh.impl.checked.vectors.body: 36 small cases, each with the exact values the rule must produce: zero holdings, editions, transfers inside one block, consolidation carry, burns, FirstGM, floors, boost tiers, rounding ties, malformed events, and inputs that must produce no result. Vectors 1 to 18 were derived by hand; 19 to 35 were generated by the reference and their derivations checked by hand. Every implementation must pass all of them.
network.tdh.impl.checked.replays.title: Differential replays.
network.tdh.impl.checked.replays.body: Whole days run through more than one implementation and compared with 6529.io’s published values. The 2026-10-11 replay reproduced 10,278 of 10,280 identities; the two others are explained (DEV-2).
network.tdh.impl.checked.dual.title: The dual run in every validator.
network.tdh.impl.checked.dual.body: Before it signs, a validator computes TDH with the Rust core and with program B. If they disagree on any value, it does not sign and raises an alarm.
network.tdh.impl.checked.daily.title: The daily comparison.
network.tdh.impl.checked.daily.body: From 16 October 2026, 6529 runs the Rust core and the Python reference every day beside 6529.io’s backend and publishes the three results.
network.tdh.impl.checked.proofs.title: Proofs.
network.tdh.impl.checked.proofs.body: Programs A and B are being built to prove each day’s result from Ethereum’s own history in two different zero-knowledge virtual machines; a minimal Ethereum contract that records proven results is built and tested on a copy of mainnet and is not deployed.
network.tdh.impl.checked.after: After the cutover, 6529.io runs the Rust core itself, so comparing the two no longer tests the computation, only its publication. The independent checks are then the Python reference and program B.
network.tdh.impl.web.title: The checks around the vectors
network.tdh.impl.web.desc: The 36 vectors sit at the centre; the Rust core, program B and the Python reference each pass 36 of 36. Around them run the dual run, the daily comparison and proofs A and B.

network.tdh.impl.vectors.title: The 36 conformance vectors
network.tdh.impl.vectors.intro: Each vector is a small input with the exact output the rule requires. The vector files are published with the source.
network.tdh.impl.vectors.caption: Conformance vectors, {shown} of 36 shown
network.tdh.impl.v.01-zero: No holdings; a consolidated pair still has a zero record
network.tdh.impl.v.02-single-erc721: One Gradient, the Gradient rate and boost
network.tdh.impl.v.03-erc1155-editions: Two editions, a zero-day copy, a half-unit final tie
network.tdh.impl.v.05-same-block-out-the: On-chain order against the old same-second rule
network.tdh.impl.v.06-consolidation-age-: Age carried inside an identity, applied to history
network.tdh.impl.v.07-consolidation-lifo: A moved old copy is removed first
network.tdh.impl.v.08-burns: Zero and dead sinks; editions not reduced; totals without sinks
network.tdh.impl.v.10-boost-tiers: Genesis, Nakamoto, season sets, full sets, Gradient cap
network.tdh.impl.v.12-rounding-boundarie: Rate, base, final and extra-set rounding boundaries
network.tdh.impl.v.14-consolidation-clus: Link states, groups of three, chains, revocations
network.tdh.impl.v.15-cutoff-and-days: Finalized snapshot with a missed slot; whole-day boundaries
network.tdh.impl.v.16-cluster-same-block: A pattern on which the old code crashes
network.tdh.impl.v.17-creation-mint-elig: A zero-amount creation mint starts the clock
network.tdh.impl.v.18-erc721-round-trip: Send and return in one transaction
network.tdh.impl.v.19-season-count: Seasons listed by the count of eligible Memes
network.tdh.impl.v.20-held-zero-day: Zero-day copies count as held for boosts
network.tdh.impl.v.22-no-eligible-meme: No eligible Meme: H = 0, minimum rates, daily rate
network.tdh.impl.v.23-identity-sums: Identity sums, a full set split across wallets, per-token finals
network.tdh.impl.v.24-ages-and-counts: Eligibility boundary, ages, counts, large ids, dead senders, many sets
network.tdh.impl.v.25-raw-log-cycle: A full day from raw events, all four delegation events
network.tdh.impl.v.26-delegation-decodin: Delegation event layouts and malformed events
network.tdh.impl.v.29-invalid-underflow: No result: a send larger than the holding
network.tdh.impl.v.30-invalid-duplicate-: No result: an event included twice
network.tdh.impl.v.31-invalid-zero-editi: No result: a held Meme with edition 0
network.tdh.impl.v.32-invalid-rate-range: No result: a rate input outside the range
network.tdh.impl.v.33-invalid-final-rang: No result: a final value outside the range
network.tdh.impl.v.34-cutoff-edges: No result before the next block is final, or with non-increasing times
